# txtai: The Full AI Framework for Semantic Search, RAG and Autonomous Agents

The video features txtai, an open source AI framework that brings together semantic search, orchestration of LLMs and workflows in a single structure. It explains the database of embeddings, which combines vector indexes, graphs and relational banks, pipelines, agents and RAG, and highlights local execution, without sending data to external services.

Video by Maurício Yokoyama Issei, published on November 21, 2026 (7 min 34 s).
Watch: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=flJnoDrNLcE

_The video and the transcript are in Portuguese. The minutes between brackets, such as [04:12], point to the excerpt of the video._

## A tool to simplify development with AI

The video features txtai, a tool created to simplify the development of artificial intelligence applications [00:00]. In a scenario where new vector tools and databases appear every day, a structure that facilitates the routine of those working with software engineering is fundamental [00:13].

The analysis has five parts [00:25]:

1. the all-in-one structure [00:25];
2. semantic search and embeddings [00:39];
3. orchestration of LLMs and pipelines [00:39];
4. workflows and autonomous agents [00:39];
5. Why choose txtai [00:39].

## The all-in-one structure

According to the video, the repository has over 13,600 stars in GitHub [00:55]. For the video, the number is not vanity: it shows the technical trust of the community in an open source project tested on real problems [01:09].

The txtai functions as a Swiss penknife for development with AI [01:21]. It replaces the work of sewing isolated databases with orchestration tools that do not talk to each other [01:35]. As it uses solid bases such as Python 3.11 and the Hugging Face ecosystem, the creation of larger applications becomes a unique and cleaner process [01:35].

## Semantic Search and Embeddings

Rather, the search depended on the exact word. If the keyword was not in the text, the result did not appear [02:02]. The semantic search changes this: the system understands the meaning and context of natural language [02:16]. He finds results that mean the same thing, even with different words [02:16].

In the database of the txtai is a database of embeddings that combines vector indexes, graph analysis and relational databases [02:29]. The differential is to accept different data types in the same search space [02:45]:

- text [02:45];
- transcribed audio [02:45];
- image and video [02:57].

It is also possible to combine complex searches with SQL [02:57].

## Orchestration of LLMs and pipelines

The central point here is the RAG, the increased generation by recovery [03:15]. Generating AI systems usually hallucinate: the model invents information and responds with confidence [03:15]. The RAG reduces this risk because it forces the model to consult a reliable knowledge base before responding [03:27]. Thus, corporate applications respond based on documented facts [03:39].

Orchestration doesn't just depend on big models. The txtai connects smaller models and specialized in pipelines, which are sequenced task chains [03:53]. The example of the video [03:53]:

1. an audio file or a PDF enters the system [03:53];
2. the text is extracted [04:07];
3. the language is detected [04:07];
4. the text is translated [04:07];
5. in the end, the system generates a summary of the content [04:07].

## Workflows and autonomous agents

Workflows are the glue of the system [04:20]. They combine business logic and orchestrate pipelines to run as large-scale processes [04:35]. Transforming a chain of models into a simple interface or a microservice gets fast [04:48].

At the highest level are the agents [04:48]. They are built on structures such as the smolagents, the Hugging Face [05:01]. Agents connect vector databases, pipelines and workflows to solve complex problems in an iterative and autonomous way [05:01]. The agent reads the context and decides which tool to use next [05:15].

## Why choose txtai

The repository documentation summarizes the philosophy of the project with the idea of "including drums" [05:27]. Almost all initial friction, such as configuring dependencies, connecting banks or climbing servers, ceases to exist [05:42]. With few lines of code, the base is ready for use and testing [05:56].

Running everything locally brings strategic advantages [05:56]:

- **privacy:** no sensitive data needs to go through third-party APIs in the cloud [06:08];
- **cost:** avoids high and unpredictable infrastructure costs [06:08];
- **scale on demand:** memory consumption is low, and hardware only grows when the project requires [06:21].

The core of the tool also offers APIs for languages other than Python, such as JavaScript, Java, Rust and Go [06:33]. For the video, this shows that architecture was designed to adapt to almost any technology ecosystem [06:47].

## A question to close

With well-composed tools running locally and isolatedly, traditional development bottlenecks decrease [07:01]. The video ends with a reflection: with an entire AI ecosystem running on a single machine, without external cloud, what will be built next [07:14]?

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What differentiates semantic search from keyword search?

The search for a keyword only finds the exact term. The semantic search understands the meaning and finds results that say the same thing in other words [02:16].

### Does txtai need cloud services?

Nope. The video highlights that everything can run locally without sending data to third party APIs [06:08].

### What are the txtai agents supporting?

In structures like the alms, Hugging Face. They connect vector banks, pipelines and workflows and choose the next tool alone [05:01].

- [GitHub - neuml/txtai: All-in-one AI framework for semantic search, LLM orchestration and language model workflows](https://github.com/neuml/txtai): Project README. Supports the description of txtai as an all-in-one framework, the database of embeddings as union of vector indexes (spars and dense), network of graphs and relational banks, vector search with SQL, indexing text, documents, audio, image and video, pipelines (questions and answers, labeling, transcription, translation, abstract), workflows, agents built on the smolagents, the RAG against hallucinations, the 'batteries included', Python 3.11+ with Hugging Face and bindings for JavaScript, Java, Rust and Go. - [Why txtai? - txtai](https://neuml.github.io/txtai/why/): Documentation page. Supports local execution without sending data to remote services ('Local Run'), low scale consumption only when accurate ('Low footprint') and built-in API to use the programming language of choice.

## About the video

O **txtai** it is a complete open source AI framework focused on semantic search, orchestration of LLMs and pipelines with language models. Developed in Python 3.11+, the framework integrates technologies such as Hugging Face Transformers, Sentence Transformers and FastAPI.

In this video, we explore the all-in-one structure of txtai and how it simplifies the development of smart applications.

📌 **What you will learn in this video:**
* **Embeddings Database Unified:** Since txtai combines vector indexes (dense and sparse), graph networks and relational databases with queries via SQL.
* **Multimodal Indexation:** Creating embeddings for texts, documents, audio, images and videos.
* **Pipelines and Workflows:** Automation of tasks such as questions and answers (QA), labeling, audio transcription, translation and summarization.
* **RAG and Autonomous Agents:** Construction of advanced Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) solutions and intelligent agents capable of connecting tools and solving complex problems.
* **Flexible execution:** Local and secure operation without mandatory sending of data to external services, with support for climbing via ready containers and APIs.
